chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man to whom I give money, saying to him: 'When I give you the money, which is fifty thousand, ten thousand dirhams of this money are a loan upon you, and the remainder remains with me; buy for me whatever you see fit with it.' I asked: 'Is this arrangement sound? Is it more preferable to you, or should I hire him for the money for a known wage?' He said: 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine a loan and a profit-sharing partnership in one financial agreement in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) validates a hybrid financial structure where a portion of capital serves as an interest-free loan (qard) while the remainder is deployed for profit-sharing or agency (mudarabah/mu'awadah). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic flexibility in combining distinct contractual forms within a single transaction, provided the components are clearly delineated, thereby offering a practical model for Islamic finance that avoids the rigidity of treating each contract in isolation.
